audit_findings.title: Convertible-note dilution does not match the equity-earnings claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $575.0m principal; 8.137m full-conversion shares versus 2.792m maximum shares for value above principal at $107.58, a 5.345m (8.5%) denominator overcount; denominator-only base-value impact +$4.42/share; cash and interest effects unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The share denominator counts principal as equity dilution even though principal must be settled in cash; consistent conversion modeling may also change available cash and OE when note interest ceases.
audit_findings.evidence: The consideration due in respect of each trading day in the Observation Period will consist of cash, up to at least the proportional amount of the principal amount being converted, and any excess of the proportional conversion value for that trading day that will not be settled in cash will be settled in shares of our common stock.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated. The 2026 notes were repaid in cash, while the remaining 2030 notes require cash settlement of at least principal. Counting their entire conversion capacity materially understates per-share value before considering the competing effects of principal settlement and discontinued interest expense.
audit_findings.action: Rerun separate all-cash and principal-cash/excess-shares cases using the adjusted conversion rate, observation-period price, cash required at settlement and interest add-back only after extinguishment.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may be receiving free reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $210m planned FY2026 total capex, 105.7% of $198.7m anchor OE; incremental growth-capex shortfall unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncharged incremental restaurant investment inflates forecast OE and growth; adding cash that must fund expansion would also overstate the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We anticipate approximately $210 million in capital expenditures to support this level of unit development, as well as required maintenance on our restaurants.
audit_findings.explanation: The model has no explicit forecast reinvestment schedule, but the record does not establish how much required investment is already embedded in anchor OE. Because planned total capex exceeds the entire OE anchor, any meaningful omitted growth component is capable of materially changing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile maintenance, new-unit, landlord-funded and operating-lease-asset expenditures by forecast year, then rerun each growth case with OE after all required reinvestment and with only surplus cash in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The terminal earnings base depends heavily on unusually favorable tax credits
audit_findings.magnitude: $35.55m FY2025 FICA-tip credit, 21.8% of pretax income and 17.9% of $198.7m anchor OE; sustainable loss unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher sustainable cash-tax rate would reduce forecast OE and the terminal earnings base.
audit_findings.evidence: If we were to not qualify for the SITCA program, as currently proposed, it could cause us to lose tax credits which could materially adversely affect our financial performance.
audit_findings.explanation: Dependence on the credit is demonstrated, while loss of qualification or a change in the credit regime remains unresolved. The filed credit is large relative to anchor OE, so perpetuating the 8.9% FY2025 effective rate without a durability finding is materially consequential.
audit_findings.action: Obtain current SITCA qualification evidence and applicable tax guidance, derive a sustainable cash-tax rate, and rerun the DCF with partial and full loss-of-credit cases.

audit_findings.title: The latest-actual anchor capitalizes a nonrecurring gift-card estimate benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.396m pretax net benefit; $6.953m after tax at the filed 26% adjustment rate; computed base-value effect -$97.7m or -$1.55/share
audit_findings.mechanism: The nonrecurring net benefit increases anchor OE and is consequently grown and capitalized through the terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Represents gift card breakage revenue of $17.3 million as a result of a change in historical redemption patterns, partially offset by a non-recurring $7.9 million write-down of gift card inventory.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a $17.3m estimate-change benefit offset by a $7.9m inventory write-down. Removing the filed net adjustment reduces the $47.53 base value by about 3.3% to approximately $45.98 per share, far short of the $60.05 gap to the $107.58 market price and insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Remove the after-tax $9.396m net adjustment from anchor OE while retaining only a demonstrated recurring level of ordinary breakage and related costs.

audit_findings.title: A one-time refinancing loss may be repeated forever
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.891m pretax; $11.759m after tax at 26%; if retained, computed base-value effect +$165.2m or +$2.63/share
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in anchor OE, the isolated extinguishment loss depresses every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: In fiscal 2025, we recorded a $15.9 million loss on early debt extinguishment.
audit_findings.explanation: The charge is demonstrated, but whether the OE reconciliation retained it is unresolved. Even assuming the entire after-tax charge was retained and capitalized, base value would rise only to approximately $50.16 per share, still $57.42 below the market price and not enough to change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the loss through the OE reconciliation; add it back once only if retained, without reversing recurring note interest or issuance-cost amortization that remains economically applicable.

audit_findings.title: The FRC contingent-payment claim is not cleanly represented in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $13.205m June 30, 2026 remaining liability; $13.229m paid in the first half of 2026; $14.449m FY2025 expense; computed bridge-only effect -$0.21/share and full FY2025 after-tax expense add-back less the liability up to +$2.18/share
audit_findings.mechanism: The unpaid claim reduces the equity bridge, while capitalizing nonrecurring remeasurement or finite compensation expense in OE understates operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The liability for this contingent consideration provision was $24.6 million at December 30, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates a remaining liability omitted from the bridge, but the recurring-versus-remeasurement composition of anchor expense remains unresolved. The bridge omission alone is 0.4% of base equity value; even the most favorable treatment of the full filed FY2025 expense produces a net increase of only about $2.18 per share, insufficient to close the $60.05 market-price gap.
audit_findings.action: Use the June 2026 liability roll-forward, separate recurring amortization from remeasurement and finite compensation, normalize anchor OE accordingly, and deduct the $13.205m remaining cash claim exactly once.
